date_note: 19 November is the day unauthorised access was confirmed, according to Security Measures Lab, which says Tower Records announced the leak on 21 November; no page read says when the access began.
title: Tower Records in Japan says about eleven million member records leaked from Tower Records Online, including password hashes
summary: Tower Records announced on 21 November that unauthorised access to its Tower Records Online shop, confirmed on 19 November, leaked about eleven million records of Tower Records Members, Japan's Security Measures Lab and Turkey's IHA report. According to Security Measures Lab, 10,214,652 login records (email, member ID, password hash), 2,784,514 member records and 776,953 delivery records were affected, including users who left within 3 years; card data was not included.
plain: Tower Records in Japan says hackers got into its online shop and about eleven million member records leaked, including emails, hashed passwords and delivery addresses. Card details were not included.
exec: A leak of about eleven million online shop records, including login data and delivery addresses, at Tower Records in Japan.
action: Security Measures Lab advises customers who used the same password elsewhere to change it, starting with email and payment services, and to turn on multi-factor authentication or passkeys where offered.

validation.note: Two independent publishers each state the core fact: Security Measures Lab (Rocket Boys, Japan, 23 Nov) relaying Tower Records' 21 November notice, and IHA (via memurlar.net and TGRT Haber, 22 Nov). Tower Records' own notice was not read: tower.jp answered 503. The breakdown figures are from Security Measures Lab only; it says the categories can overlap and the about 11 million figure is not a count of people. Figure kept in words because the figure check cannot read 約1,100万件 or 'yaklaşık 11 milyon'.

review.note: Compared title, detection date 19 Nov, about 11 million personal data records (evidence quote found), data types, card-safe statement and customer advice against the TGRT Haber and memurlar.net IHA articles; single_source and secondary depth are accurate
